title: Offline-capable zero-trust policy, key and replication enforcement for tagged data at the tactical edge (ZT Data Pillar under DDIL)
problem: Zero-trust access control and TDF-style object protection assume a reachable identity provider, policy decision point and key server, and edge data meshes that replicate through outages do not converge state while enforcing per-attribute classification, releasability and role rules, so disconnected units either fall back to implicit trust (local accounts, enclave-only protection) or lose access to protected data.

user.exact_role: Battalion/brigade S6 network and data managers who administer NGC2 tactical-cloud (hub/spoke) nodes; division data-layer administrators; expeditionary targeting and intelligence cells that must open and share tagged data during comms outages; coalition MPE/IMN operators and foreign disclosure officers who hand-tag releasability
user.echelon: Battalion through division, plus coalition tactical enclaves
organization_examples: USINDOPACOM J6 / INDOPACOM Mission Network operators (Balikatan 2026)
Navy PEO C4I PMW 790 shore/expeditionary sites
DEVCOM C5ISR Center ESI Directorate (DUCES RFI sponsor)

current_workflow: 1) When connected, users authenticate to the enterprise IdP (Army EICAM / Navy Flank Speed / Entra) and the network enclave, not object tags, is the primary protection for tactical data.

2) Data is replicated inside one vendor mesh (Lattice Mesh, Raft data platform, Ditto, TAK Server federation) using that vendor's conflict rules; access rules are coarse role permissions configured per application.

3) When the link drops, applications continue on cached credentials or local accounts with static permissions; TDF/ZTDF-wrapped objects whose keys sit on an enterprise key access service cannot be opened unless a key was cached beforehand.

4) Cross-enclave or cross-partner movement goes through an accredited cross-domain solution after a foreign-disclosure officer or JICO hand-tags the data, or the product is re-typed by hand on the releasable enclave (WFX 24-03, Balikatan 2026).
5) On reconnection, duplicates and stale objects are reconciled manually or ignored; audit logs are backfilled by hand; revocations issued during the outage were not enforced at the edge.
current_solution: Enterprise ZT stacks (DISA Thunderdome, Navy Flank Speed, Army EICAM) extended toward the edge with periodic SATCOM; an Army Tactical-ICAM (T-ICAM) prototype OTA for DDIL identity (identity pillar only); Xage Fabric marketed as DDIL-tolerant access enforcement (vendor claim); Virtru/OpenTDF ZTDF objects with a cloud/enterprise Key Access Service and vendor-claimed offline TDF creation; Anduril Lattice Mesh / Raft / Ditto for outage-tolerant replication without label-aware policy; accredited CDS guards (Everfox, Owl, GDMS BICES) at enclave boundaries; manual FDO tagging.
failure: Enforcement and availability trade off at the moment of disconnection: either the edge keeps working on implicit trust (Army CTO memo on NGC2: 'we cannot control who sees what, we cannot see what users are doing') or protected objects become unreadable because no local policy decision point / key authority exists; attributes and revocations go stale while disconnected; replication engines converge data without evaluating releasability, so guards at re-connection apply the most restrictive rule and data is delayed or lost; and no two vendor meshes converge with each other.

evidence.claim: DEVCOM C5ISR Center ESI Directorate issued the 'Tactical Data in Use Security' (DUCES) RFI seeking DoD Zero Trust Data Pillar capabilities that 'integrate seamlessly into existing infrastructure' and 'operate within a denied, degraded, intermittent, or limited (DDIL) contested communications, logistics, and information environment', asking for encryption, anomaly detection and secure communication protocols; the deadline was later extended. No public prototype award or follow-on solicitation for DUCES was found as of 2026-09.
evidence.source_title: Army says DUCES to cyber hackers: New RFI looks for tactical edge zero trust solutions (Breaking Defense); Army extends deadline for Tactical Data in Use Security RFI (Intelligence Community News); SAM.gov notice
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy SBIR 24.4 NAVWAR Open Topic N244-P03 'Advanced Data Integrity and Control Methods' cites ICDF and ZTDF as data formats that embed control in the elemental object and requires solutions to 'protect data independent of networks, applications, or database technologies, function in disrupted, disconnected, intermittent and low-bandwidth (DDIL) situations, and recover gracefully once connectivity is restored'; the Navy FY26 Release 3 topic DON26BZ03-NV059 'Real-time Zero Trust Data and Access Control for Combat Systems' (pre-release 2026-06-03, closed 2026-07-22, Phase I up to $315k) again requires resilience 'in degraded environments where communications infrastructure may be compromised'. Two cycles of the same ask across NAVWAR and combat-systems sponsors = repeated procurement of research, not production.
evidence.source_title: Navy 24.4 SBIR NAVWAR Open Topic N244-P03 (navysbir.com); sbir.gov topic 10735; DON26BZ03-NV059 (navysbir.com); sbir.gov topic 12755

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The problem sits at the intersection of three specialties that rarely coexist in one small team: applied cryptography/key management (delegated, time-boxed key release with offline revocation semantics), distributed-systems theory (label-carrying CRDTs with deterministic, policy-respecting merge), and DoD labeling/releasability policy (CAPCO/ISM, STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240, foreign-disclosure rules). The ZT vendors (Xage, Virtru) come from enterprise/OT identity and object encryption and have solved 'keep working when the link drops' for their own product, not policy-aware convergence across meshes; the mesh vendors (Anduril, Ditto, Raft) have solved convergence but treat access policy as an application concern (the Army CTO memo documents the result); CDS vendors solve the boundary, not the interior. The only named sponsor so far (DEVCOM C5ISR ESI) is an S&T organization issuing an RFI, not a PEO with production dollars, and the Navy has bought it only as SBIR topics - so there has been no production pull to justify a focused company. Finally, real labeled data and NSA-approved crypto integration require cleared U.S. persons, which filters out most early-stage teams.
technical_wedge: An 'edge policy and key node' that a tactical-cloud hub or TAK Server can run: (1) an OpenTDF-compatible Key Access Service and policy decision point that pre-fetches signed, time-boxed attribute bundles and key grants for the unit's expected users and data while connected; (2) offline ABAC enforcement on ZTDF/IC-TDF objects with explicit grant expiry, local revocation lists and tamper-evident local audit; (3) label-carrying replicated data types whose sync filters are derived from the same policy, so a node only stores and forwards objects its holders are cleared/releasable to see, with deterministic merge and provenance; (4) reconciliation on reconnect (audit upload, revocation catch-up, key rotation). Packaged as an open-core library/sidecar (TAK plugin, Kubernetes sidecar for UDS/Zarf-style edge stacks, Lattice SDK adapter) rather than a platform, so both NGC2 primes could embed it.

mvp.what: Two-tier demo: an 'enterprise' OpenTDF platform (KAS + attribute authority + OIDC IdP) on a laptop, and an edge node (second laptop or small compute) running the offline PDP/KAS and a label-aware sync engine feeding ATAK-CIV/TAK Server; synthetic CoT/USMTF messages tagged US-only, REL FVEY and REL NATO.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Cut the link: show continued policy-correct open/deny for pre-provisioned users, correct denial after a simulated revocation, and grant expiry; partition three edge nodes with different releasability and show convergence with zero leakage and measured bandwidth; reconnect and replay audit/revocation. Publish the leakage, convergence-time and bandwidth measurements plus an open-source library.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: Zero unauthorized reads across partitions (formal or fuzzed), bounded staleness of attributes/revocations, convergence without manual de-duplication, acceptable overhead on a tactical-radio-class link (tens of kbit/s), and that it is a thin add-on to OpenTDF/TAK rather than a new platform.

data_requirement.what: Synthetic tactical messages and files with realistic labels; the marking/attribute schemas (ISM/CAPCO-style, STANAG 4774 confidentiality labels, ACP-240 attributes); later, government-furnished attribute feeds and exercise captures under a CRADA/OTA.

Real labeled operational data is classified or CUI and only obtainable inside a sponsored experiment with cleared U.S.-person staff - a non-U.S.-person founder should assume no access.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. small business >50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; a German founder who becomes a permanent resident can count toward that, the Indonesian founder (not a U.S. person) cannot, so ownership must be structured with counsel and any U.S.-person employees/investors matter. incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes for the access-control and audit pieces: Anduril already announced ZT capabilities on Lattice/Menace with Booz Allen (May 2026) and Palantir has mature ABAC/markings inside Foundry; Virtru could ship an edge KAS; Xage could add object-level policy. The hard, unglamorous part - label-aware convergent replication across two vendors' meshes with offline key/revocation semantics - is something each prime would prefer to solve only inside its own mesh, which is exactly the vendor-neutral seam the Army says it wants government-owned APIs for.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it (a) ships an open, standards-anchored (OpenTDF/TAK) component that both NGC2 teams can embed cheaply, (b) gets a government sponsor (C5ISR ESI, ZT PfMO, PMW 790) to reference it in ZT activity guidance or an NGC2 API baseline, and (c) proves zero-leakage convergence with published measurements primes cannot match without re-architecting. Reject if the Booz Allen-Anduril integration or T-ICAM demonstrably closes the DDIL policy/key gap by 2027, or if the Army accepts enclave-plus-cached-identity as target-level compliance - both are plausible.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Cryptographic key-management software is export-controlled (EAR Category 5 Part 2 at minimum, possibly ITAR USML Category XI(b)/XIII(b) if specially designed for military use) - classification requires counsel; any integration with NSA-approved high-assurance encryption (an explicit NGC2 requirement in the FY26 NDAA) or with classified attribute data requires cleared U.S. persons and potentially a facility clearance with FOCI mitigation; production use requires an ATO/cATO under RMF (SWFT/cATO reforms help); the SBIR path requires >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership and control. Interoperable data tagging itself is still being socialized by the DoD CIO ZT PfMO (webinars 2024-2025), so the policy the product enforces is a moving target.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder should be assumed unable to access ITAR technical data, controlled crypto source under deemed-export rules without a license, classified or CUI attribute data, or exercise networks; the German founder's permanent residency helps SBIR ownership and deemed-export status but a permanent resident is still a 'foreign interest' for FOCI purposes under 32 CFR 117.11 if a facility clearance is sought. Product architecture should keep the open, non-controlled core (label-aware CRDT library, OpenTDF-compatible policy logic on public specs) separable from controlled crypto and government-furnished components. Describe as constraints requiring counsel, not legal conclusions.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Offline-capable attribute-based key release and policy-aware sync map to commercial 'sovereign' and OT/IoT problems (mining, maritime, energy, disaster response, healthcare devices in disconnected sites, cross-company data rooms), and OpenTDF already has commercial users via Virtru. But commercial buyers rarely need multi-releasability convergence; the commercial analogue is closer to Ditto's or Xage's existing markets, so dual-use revenue is plausible but would be won against those incumbents, not on defense-specific features.

defensibility.explanation: The label-aware merge/filter algorithms and their verified leakage properties, the accredited edge KAS/PDP package (ATO artifacts, FIPS-validated build), embedded integrations inside TAK Server and the NGC2 data layer, and sponsor relationships (C5ISR ESI, ZT PfMO, PMW 790) are the assets. The open format (ZTDF) is deliberately not proprietary; defensibility comes from being the accredited, embedded reference implementation - an OpenTDF-style position that holds only if a government sponsor treats it as the standard component. Without that, it is a feature primes copy.

why_now: Four dated forces converge in 2025-2027: (1) the DoD ZT target-level deadline of 30 Sep 2027 with NSA ZIGs (Jan 2026) and an April 2026 ZIG update naming ZTDF/IC-TDF; (2) NGC2 moving from prototype to a designated common data baseline (June 2026) and I Corps scaling, after an Army CTO memo (Sept 2025) documented missing access control; (3) Congress tying NGC2 money to DDIL resiliency and NSA-approved crypto (FY26 NDAA); (4) the first Army RFI (DUCES, Feb 2025) and two Navy SBIR cycles (24.4 and FY26 R3) explicitly asking for data-pillar protection that works disconnected. Technically, OpenTDF matured as an open KAS/attribute stack and CRDT tooling became production-grade, so a small team can build on open baselines rather than inventing formats.
killer_risk: The most likely outcome is that the gap gets absorbed rather than bought: the Army accepts cached identity (T-ICAM) plus network enclaves plus a CDS at the boundary as target-level compliance for tactical systems, Anduril/Booz Allen and Palantir bundle 'zero trust' inside the NGC2 data layer at no incremental price, and Virtru adds an edge KAS - leaving a two-founder company with SBIR-sized research contracts, no program office that owns the requirement, export-control friction on its core code, and a founder who cannot touch the data the product is meant to protect.

allied_extension: More compelling, with caveats. The strongest documented pain is coalition (Balikatan 2026 hand-tagging, WFX 24-03 regeneration at lower enclave, U.S.-Japan 'emails and PDFs', GAO-25-106454), and the relevant standards (STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240, NATO data-centric security) are allied by construction; NATO DIANA accepts companies domiciled in any NATO nation regardless of founder nationality, and Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN programmes (delivery 2026-2029) will need label-aware edge data services for a mixed analogue/digital force. Caveats: allied buyers procure through primes (Rheinmetall, Thales, blackned), NATO data-centric security is itself still maturing, and a product accredited for U.S. NSA-approved crypto cannot simply be exported - the allied version would need a separate, non-ITAR build. For a German-Indonesian team an EU/NATO-domiciled entity may be the lower-friction first market for this specific gap, but the U.S. demand signals are the only dated, funded ones found.
